facts_known: Reported 16 Nov 2026 by WhatsApp from unit C-12-03, Block C, floor 12 (occupied, tenant, 10 share units).
Incident reported Monday 16 November 2026, about 7.45 a.m., Block C car park entrance.
Resident reports the car park barrier came down on her car and scratched the bonnet.
Resident asks the management to pay RM 850 for a respray.
Resident's phone number is recorded by the officer (call-back requested).
facts_missing: Source of the barrier incident: the resident has not said which unit or person was involved; this is only what she believes, and nothing has been verified.
Whether the barrier was faulty or malfunctioned, or was operated by a person, and whether the guard was on duty.
Vehicle registration number and bay number.
Whether the car belongs to the resident or to the owner of C-12-03 (she is a tenant).
Photographs of the scratch and of the barrier, and any repair quote or invoice behind the RM 850 figure.
Whether any other vehicle or person was affected or any incident was recorded at the guardhouse.

next_steps.action: Acknowledge the WhatsApp message today or by the next working day, by WhatsApp, using the draft reply.

Record the facts above. Ask the resident for the vehicle registration number, bay number, photos, the repair quote or invoice, and whether the car is hers or the owner's. Do not name or act against any person or unit on the unverified report.

Ask the guard on duty to check the Block C car park entrance barrier on site and record what was seen, with date and time, and whether the barrier is working correctly and whether an incident was logged that morning.
If the check shows a fault in the barrier (common property), log a maintenance work order and give the resident the reference number. If no fault is found, record that and say so to the resident.

Hand the RM 850 claim to the building manager with the handover note. The documents in the office do not show any rule that makes the management corporation pay for damage to a vehicle by the barrier, so the claim is for the building manager to decide. Do not agree, refuse or estimate the amount to the resident.

guidance.draft_reply:
Thank you for your WhatsApp message about your car at the Block C car park entrance on Monday 16 November at about 7.45 a.m. We have asked our guard to check the barrier on site, and we will log a maintenance work order and send you the reference number if a fault is found. Your request for RM 850 has been passed to the building manager, who will reply to you; passing it on does not mean the claim has been accepted. Please send your car's registration number, photos of the scratch and the barrier, and any repair quote or invoice, and tell us whether the car is yours or the owner's.

Management Office, Amber Residences
